rationale: Evidence: iteration 3 (base_speed 1.1, kd 0.5) scored 471.07, the best so far. Iteration 4 changed only base_speed to 1.0 and scored 445.98. That change did not help. The oval fell from 20/20 to 19/20 finishes, and the s-bend max_error rose from 0.0598 m to 0.0628 m, so speed is not the lever at this point. Across speeds 1.3, 1.1 and 1.0, s-bend max_error was 0.0613, 0.0598 and 0.0628, so it sits at the 0.06 m off-track limit regardless of speed. The slalom has 0 finishes and 0 line-loss events at every speed, so line loss is not the cause. The Evaluator's approved entityR1 is the iteration 4 design, which scored lower than iteration 3, so I am not reusing it. Change: return base_speed to 1.1, the best-scoring value, and keep the iteration 3 geometry (sensors x -0.06 to +0.06 in 0.03 m steps at y 0.05, size 0.012). Raise kd from 0.5 to 0.7 as the single controller change, as the Evaluator suggested, so the damping effect is isolated. kd has not been varied on its own. Hypothesis: the s-bend steering_oscillation of about 0.31 at kd 0.5 indicates overshoot in bends, and more derivative action should pull the peak error below 0.06 m. Expected result: s-bend and slalom max_error below 0.06 m, more s-bend finishes, and the oval still finishing near 2.0 s. Risks: higher kd may increase jitter on the oval, and if it does, I will return kd to 0.5 and try kp 1.4 next. Measurements wanted next: per-track finish rate, max_error, steering_oscillation, and completion_time, to check whether kd reduces bend overshoot.
